title: Ezra the scribe read the Torah before all the people in front of the Water Gate, and public Torah reading became linked to his name

trailer.text: Ezra, called in Scripture the scribe and the priest, ascended from Babylonia to the community in Judea, and the Rabbis compared him to Moshe Rabbeinu.
According to a shiur at Yeshivat Har Etzion, Ezra the scribe is one of three whom the Talmud credits for ensuring that the Torah was not forgotten, together with Hillel and R. Chiya.
According to Nehemiah chapter eight, the entire people assembled as one man in the square before the Water Gate and asked Ezra to bring the scroll of the Teaching of Moses.
Ezra read from the Torah from the first light until midday, before men and women, and the Levites explained the Torah to the people.
According to Scripture, the whole community that returned from the captivity made booths, and there was very great joy.
According to the Har Etzion shiur, the gemara in Bava Kama attributes the institution of Torah reading to the edicts of Moshe and Ezra.

stations.title: A people that asked to hear

paragraphs.text: According to the Har Etzion shiur, the historical background points to mass ignorance among the remnant in Judea.
According to the shiur, the laws of building a sukkah were unfamiliar to the people.
According to the shiur, it is not clear that the Judean community would have learned the basics of the Torah had Ezra not ascended from Babylonia.
According to Nehemiah chapter eight, the entire people assembled as one man in the square before the Water Gate.
According to the Har Etzion shiur, this place is southeast of the Temple Mount.
The people asked Ezra the scribe to bring the scroll of the Teaching of Moses with which the LORD had charged Israel.
According to the Har Etzion shiur, this request by the people demonstrates a partnership between the religious leadership and the public in spreading the Torah.

stations.title: The wooden tower and the open scroll

paragraphs.text: On the first day of the seventh month, Ezra the priest brought the Teaching before the congregation, men and women and all who could listen with understanding.
Ezra stood upon a wooden tower made for the purpose.
At his right stood six men: Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah.
According to the Har Etzion shiur, at his left stood seven more.
Ezra opened the scroll in the sight of all the people, for he was above all the people.
As he opened the scroll, all the people stood up.
Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God.
All the people answered, “Amen, Amen,” with hands upraised.
Ezra read from the Torah from the first light until midday.
Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah and others, as well as the Levites, explained the Torah to the people, while the people stood in their places.
The readers read from the scroll of the Teaching of God, translating it and giving the sense.
So the people understood the reading.
According to the Har Etzion shiur, it would appear from the need for translators that the people did not understand Hebrew.
According to the shiur, the root “bina” appears six times in the chapter, and the chapter emphasizes study.

stations.title: From weeping to joy, and from joy to booths

paragraphs.text: All the people wept as they heard the words of the Torah.
Nehemiah, Ezra and the Levites told the people that the day was holy, and that they must not mourn or weep.
The people were told to go and eat choice foods, drink sweet drinks, and send portions to whoever had nothing prepared.
All the people went to eat, drink, send portions and make great merriment, for they understood the things they were told.
On the second day, the heads of the clans, the priests and the Levites gathered to Ezra the scribe to study the words of the Torah.
The people went out, brought branches, and made booths on the roofs, in the courtyards, in the courtyards of the House of God, and in the squares of the Water Gate and the Ephraim Gate.
According to Scripture, the Israelites had not done so from the days of Joshua son of Nun to that day.
According to an article on TheTorah.com, the people here learn together, discover the commandment of the festival, and act upon what they learned.

stations.title: From the square to the synagogue

paragraphs.text: According to an article on TheTorah.com, in the Septuagint the word “ויאספו” was translated with a Greek verb from which the word “synagogue” is derived.
According to the article, the lifting of the Torah scroll in the synagogue is done after the reading, or, following Ezra, before it.
According to the Har Etzion shiur, many laws of Torah reading were derived from the chapter, among them the lifting of the Torah scroll.
According to the shiur, Ralbag holds that Ezra's blessing is the basis for the blessings recited upon the reading of the Torah.
According to the Har Etzion shiur, Ezra's ceremony was intended to recreate the Hakhel ceremony described in Sefer Devarim.
According to the shiur, the mishna in Sota records that during the Hakhel ceremony the king read the Torah from a wooden platform, and it appears that this was learned from Ezra.
According to the shiur, there is substantial evidence that Hakhel is a recreation of the Revelation at Sinai, once every seven years.
According to an article on TheTorah.com, Yehezkel Kaufmann called Tishrei the “month of Torah.”

According to the Har Etzion shiur, there is a dispute among the Tanna’im as to whether Hakhel is performed on the Temple Mount or in the Women’s Courtyard, and the dispute concerns the reading of the verses in Nehemiah.
According to the baraita in Bava Kama, Ezra instituted ten enactments, among them reading at Minchah on Shabbat and reading on Monday and Thursday.
According to the gemara there, Ezra instituted that three men read ten verses.
According to the gemara, the courts sit in judgment on Monday and Thursday, because people come then to hear the reading of the scroll.

According to a baraita in Tractate Megillah, Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said that Ezra instituted the reading of the curses of Torat Kohanim before Shavuot and the curses of Mishneh Torah before Rosh Hashanah.
According to the Har Etzion shiur, the chapter presents the Torah reading as a transformative event of Shivat Tzion, and even of Jewish history.
According to the shiur, the people were profoundly impacted by their renewed exposure to the Torah.
According to the shiur, the Rabbis compared Ezra to Moshe Rabbeinu, and gave Ezra an equal share in transmitting the tradition.
According to the shiur, the gemara in Sanhedrin states that had Moshe not preceded him, Ezra would have been fit to give the Torah to the Jewish People.

According to the Har Etzion shiur, the Sigd holiday of Ethiopian Jews, which the Knesset adopted in 2008 as a national Israeli holiday, is linked to the events of Nehemiah and to the Revelation at Sinai.

According to the Har Etzion shiur, this is the only chapter in which Ezra and Nechemia appear together, and some scholars have concluded from this that the event is not historical, but the shiur rejects this claim.
Therefore some scholars speculate that the event is ahistorical.
The shiur rejects this claim.

According to the shiur, to reconcile the fact that both Ezra chapter two and Nechemia chapter seven end with the people settling in their cities in the seventh month, the Malbim proposed, as one of two possibilities and not the one he prefers, that Ezra came to the Land of Israel twice, once in the time of Zerubavel and again under the leadership of Nechemia.
The shiur holds that the hypothesis is unlikely, and Malbim himself notes the difficulty.

disagreements.question: Did Ezra come to the Land of Israel twice?

versions.says: According to the Har Etzion shiur, the Malbim proposed as one possibility that Ezra came twice, once in the time of Zerubavel and once under the leadership of Nechemia, but the Malbim himself notes that this explanation is difficult and prefers another explanation.
The Har Etzion shiur: there is no hard evidence for this, and the hypothesis seems unlikely
The Talmud, Rashi, Metzudat David and Malbim, according to the Har Etzion shiur: “amdu” means they fell silent
Ibn Ezra, according to the Har Etzion shiur: the people literally stood, and perhaps this is the source of the requirement to stand when the Torah scroll is in motion

disagreements.question: Who instituted the reading on Monday and Thursday?

versions.says: The baraita in Bava Kama: Ezra, as one of his ten enactments
The gemara in Bava Kama: the reading already existed before Ezra, because prophets instituted it

claims.quote: One obvious law derived from our chapter is that of hagba, lifting the Torah.

claims.text: לפי שיעור הר עציון, הגמרא בסנהדרין קובעת שאלמלא קדם לו משה, עזרא היה ראוי שתינתן התורה על ידו לעם ישראל.
claims.quote: had Moshe not preceded him, Ezra would have been fit to give the Torah to the Jewish People

claims.text: לפי שיעור הר עציון, חג הסיגד האתיופי, שהכנסת אימצה ב-2008 כחג לאומי ישראלי, מקושר לאירועי נחמיה ולמעמד סיני.
claims.quote: Sigd, celebrated on 29 Cheshvan each year and adopted by the Kenesset as a national Israeli holiday in 2008

claims.text: לפי שיעור הר עציון, פרק זה הוא היחיד שבו עזרא ונחמיה מופיעים יחד, וחוקרים מסוימים משערים לכן שהאירוע אינו היסטורי; השיעור דוחה טענה זו.
claims.quote: our chapter is the only one in which Ezra and Nechemia appear together, leading some scholars to speculate that the event is ahistorical.

claims.text: לפי שיעור הר עציון, המלבי"ם הציע שעזרא עלה לארץ ישראל פעמיים, פעם בימי זרובבל ופעם בהנהגת נחמיה.
claims.quote: he proposes that in fact Ezra came twice to Israel, once in the time of Zerubavel and again under the leadership of Nechemia.

claims.text: לפי שיעור הר עציון, אין ראיה חותכת לכך שעזרא עלה פעמיים, ולכן ההשערה נראית בלתי סבירה; המלבי"ם עצמו מציין את הקושי.
claims.quote: given that there is no hard evidence that Ezra came twice to Israel, such a hypothesis seems unlikely.

claims.text: לפי שיעור הר עציון, התלמוד (סוטה לט ע"א), רש"י, מצודת דוד והמלבי"ם מפרשים את "עמדו" כשתיקה ולא כעמידה.
claims.quote: The Talmud (Sota 39a), however, followed by Rashi, Metzudat David, and Malbim, interprets the word “amdu” as denoting silence, not standing.

claims.text: לפי שיעור הר עציון, אבן עזרא סבור שהעם עמד ממש, ולכן הפסוק רומז אולי לדרישה לעמוד כשספר התורה בתנועה.
claims.quote: Still, Ibn Ezra proposes that the people literally stood up

claims.text: לפי הגמרא בבבא קמא, הקריאה בשני ובחמישי הייתה קיימת עוד קודם עזרא, שכן נביאים תיקנו אותה מוקדם יותר.
claims.quote: עָמְדוּ נְבִיאִים שֶׁבֵּינֵיהֶם וְתִיקְּנוּ לָהֶם שֶׁיְּהוּ קוֹרִין בַּשַּׁבָּת

claims.text: לפי מאמר ב-TheTorah.com, מן הטקסט לא ברור מה העם, או נחמיה, חושבים שהחג הזה הוא.
claims.quote: It is unclear from the text what the people—or Nehemiah—think this holiday is.

quote_translations.c51: Ezra instituted ten enactments: that one reads at Minchah on Shabbat, and reads on Monday and Thursday, and courts judge on Monday and Thursday, and one launders on Thursday, and one eats garlic on Shabbat eve
quote_translations.c45: It is noteworthy that in the Septuagint to Neh. 8:1, the word ויאספו is translated συνήχθησαν, the aorist passive of the verb συνάγω
quote_translations.c53: He came and instituted three men and ten verses, corresponding to ten idlers
quote_translations.c54: And courts judge on Monday and Thursday – because people are commonly present, as they come to hear the reading of the scroll
quote_translations.c55: Ezra instituted for Israel that they should read the curses in Torat Kohanim before Atzeret, and those in Mishneh Torah before Rosh Hashanah
quote_translations.c52: The prophets among them arose and instituted for them that they should read on Shabbat
